cells.tense: Right now you're in the conditions, meeting what's actually there in front of you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you carried through a bad patch, then stop on purpose tonight — one ordinary evening held whole, finished without a replacement.
cells.core:
This is your own project and you're in the middle of it with your hands. Attention goes to what's on the table, not to what might be. A version fails and you drop it and try the next, and that isn't a wound for you — it's how the thing gets built. The trouble stays the size it is.

What you've grown is feeding you while it still needs you. You know which parts are solid and which are still soft, and the next move isn't far off. There's room to try it badly first, correct it, and keep the work on its feet. The testing answers itself and you're still glad to be inside it.
cells.sheetLine: You're inside the work, and you know what's solid.
cells.verb: staying with something long enough to find out what it holds, letting the wrong version go as you go
cells.place: a dark road where you can see one step ahead and not the next

cells.tense: You're already living past a deadline that hasn't arrived, bracing for a moment nobody handed you.
cells.ask: Leave one thing tonight at the point where you'd normally check it once more, and don't look at it again until morning.
cells.core:
A finish sits in front of you and you're past it, in the next round of tests before anyone asked, adjusting something that was already done. The extra pass isn't buying much. The grip has gotten tighter than the work needs, and your hand is still out in front of the table.

Loosening the hold isn't quitting. The one check that's enough, the next version chosen on purpose, stopping because the work is done — that's the shape this takes when it's not straining. A thing gets called done long enough for hands to come off it. Set one piece down and leave it overnight.

cells.tense: You left a decision at a door you've already walked past, and you keep the question open.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you sidestepped and make it small and binding this week — schedule it or say it out loud, forward motion even if wrong.
cells.core:
Something sits and the moving has stopped. No new version gets tried, no answer gets tested against anything, and the question stays open past the point where it could be answered. The work still matters. The grip on it has gone slack rather than tight.

A next step in the dark is what's wanted — short, one move, enough light for that and no more. That's how this seat usually works: small steps taken without the whole road visible, and the road showing up as you go. Hold steady what you have for someone else, and bind one thing to a day.

cells.tense: You're already holding to something you said you weren't sure about, and no name is on it.
cells.ask: Put a name on one thing you keep showing up for and say out loud what it's produced, so the care gets its own address.
cells.core:
Meals, rides, calls, showing up — the choice already happened in the doing, and the story you tell still has you on the fence about whether it counts. The staying is real. What's grown from it is real too, and nobody has signed the work.

Saying what you tend and why, so the meals and calls belong to a choice claimed out loud, is the shape underneath this one. Claiming it is a small sentence, not a ceremony. Say what you've kept for, in your own words, to one person who saw part of it, and let the care have an address.

attempts.check: The record calls Dedication 'Faith through Intent' and 'release through completion,' so the Too Much cell risks saying the person is secretly exhausted or afraid of finishing; nothing in the record locates a feeling or its cause, so I name the gesture ('keep going,' 'don't call it done') and not the reason. A reader could reasonably say the doing is just real work and there's nothing to release, which is why the ask has to be something done anyway — a deliberate stop, one normal evening kept whole — and not a claim about needing rest. The ask survives that objection because a real deadline or unfinished build doesn't cancel it; there's still one unnamed thing that could stop. The sentence that would serve me more than the person is any version of 'you're braced,' 'you're running,' 'you're strong' — so the cells leave the person's story for them to say and just describe the hand in the middle of a reach.
